conviction_note: abs_move 5.5 (event-implied 5.48, ATM spread 50% of mid so indicative; median own reaction 4.11; FY margin guide is genuinely in play) times a p_up of 51: a soft EPS bar, a lowered consensus, rising short interest and better-than-assumed Q3 LVP point up, while 5 of the last 7 prints were sold (including Q3 2025, a record quarter, at -2.62) and raw-material inflation puts the 10.5-11% guide at risk, so the findings sum to +0.30 and the scaled number is near zero; the two measurements agree in being small.
bar: Autoliv's own collected consensus, updated 2026-10-19, 20 analysts: Q3 2026 sales $2,718m (range 2,638-2,765), adj EBIT $253m, adj EBIT margin 9.3% (9.1-9.6), EPS $2.18 (1.83-2.40); FY2026 adj EBIT margin 10.4% (below the company guide of around 10.5-11%), Q4 adj EBIT margin 13.9%. https://www.autoliv.com/investors/consensus-estimates . Company guide (Q2 release 2026-07-17): Q3 adj operating margin 'around the first half 2026 level' (H1 = 9.3%), FY organic ~0%, adj op margin ~10.5-11%, LVP -2.5%, raw material gross headwind ~$110m. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001034670/000119312526306698/alv-ex99_1.htm . Second estimate source: Benzinga Q3 EPS $2.21 / revenue $2.72bn (snippet only, page 403). Two sources plus a company guide agree on the margin bar, so the bar is sourced.
positioning_check: MarketBeat short interest, record date 2026-09-30 (published 2026-10-09): 4,931,143 shares short, 6.76% of float, 6.2 days to cover, up 7.29% from 4,595,987 at the prior record; a year earlier (2025-09-30) it was ~2.5% of float and 3.1 days, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/ALV/short-interest/ . Baseline skew_25d -2.83 vol points (25d call IV above put IV: upside paid), put/call OI 1.37 on thin OI (1,719), run-up +4.71% over 5 sessions and +3.13% over 20, spot 9.6% below the 52-week high. Short base is elevated for a large-cap supplier and building, but not crowded in the 18-23% squeeze sense.

findings.finding: The consensus EPS bar ($2.18, Autoliv consensus page 2026-10-19) sits about 5% below what the same consensus adj EBIT ($253m) converts to: Q3 2025 turned $271m adj EBIT into $2.32 adj EPS on ~77m shares, and shares outstanding fell from 73,237,217 (10 July 2026) to 72,006,695 (30 Sept 2026, 1,232,671 retired in Q3), so an in-line $253m EBIT maps to roughly $2.28-2.32 adj EPS; the EPS low of $1.83 suggests some estimates in the average are not on an adjusted basis.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name sells headline quarters: Q2 2026 (adj EPS $2.43, record Q2 sales, guide kept) -3.78; Q3 2025 (record Q3 sales, op income and EPS) -2.62; 5 of the last 7 reactions negative, the two positives both Q1 prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Wire headlines will compare reported adj EPS to the $2.18 average; a stale or GAAP-mixed estimate in that average makes an in-line EBIT read as a 'beat'. If the market had arbitraged it, the EPS consensus would sit at ~$2.30 alongside the $253m EBIT, which it does not. Partly priced by anyone who models EBIT, which the sell side does, hence small.
findings.independence: Share count from Autoliv's 30 Sept 2026 share-retirement release (https://www.inderes.se/en/releases/autoliv-retires-repurchased-shares-decreases-number-of-issued-shares-12) and the Q2 10-Q cover (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001034670/000119312526306974/alv-20260630.htm); Q3 2025 EBIT-to-EPS conversion from https://www.autoliv.com/press/financial-report-july-september-2025-2397395 . Consensus drifted down from ~$2.26 (July 22 snapshot) to $2.18, i.e. the bar was lowered: https://www.autoliv.com/es/node/565 (snippet).

findings.finding: S&P Global Mobility puts Q3 2026 global light-vehicle production at -1.6% y/y (cited in Valeo's Q3 sales release, 2026-10-22), better than the ~-3% H2 run-rate implied by Autoliv's FY assumption of -2.5% after H1 (Q1 -3.4%, Q2 -0.3%); but the regional split derived from Valeo's table (North America ~-5%, China ~-6%, Europe ~0%, Asia ex-China ~+4.5%, South America ~+6%) hits the Americas, where Autoliv underperformed LVP by 4.9pp in Q2 (32% of sales), so applying Q2's regional outperformance gives organic roughly -0.5% to 0% and sales near, perhaps ~0.5% below, the $2,718m bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 organic +3.9% trailed LVP +4.6% and the stock fell -2.62; Q1 2026 organic +0.8% vs LVP -3.4% (4.2pp outperformance) bought +6.82; Q2 2026 outperformance ~1.3pp with Americas -4.9pp sold -3.78. Outperformance vs LVP is the line this name trades on at the top line.
findings.why_not_priced: The S&P quarterly actual reached the public only via Valeo's release the evening before Autoliv reports; consensus sales ($2,718m, updated 10-19) predates it. If priced, auto-supplier estimates would have been revised in the last day; Autoliv's consensus page shows no update after 10-19. Proxy: regional figures are derived (Valeo LFL minus its stated outperformance), not published by S&P.
findings.independence: Regional Autoliv outperformance pattern and 32/30/19/19 regional mix from Autoliv's own Q2 2026 release and call (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001034670/000119312526306698/alv-ex99_1.htm ; https://www.autoliv.com/sites/autoliv/files/pr/Autoliv_Q2_2026_webcast_transcript.pdf). Shares the Valeo document with the Valeo peer finding below (different line: volume here, guidance there). GM's own NA wholesale +3.6% (finding below) cuts against the derived NA -5%.

findings.finding: Raw-material inflation from the Persian Gulf conflict did not ease in Q3 and Autoliv named helium (an airbag-inflator input) as the main driver: Autoliv's gross headwind estimate rose from ~$90m (Q1 call) to ~$110m (Q2), Nippon Sanso raised helium prices >30% from July 2026, and Hormuz commodity transits were 4 vessels on 15 Sept against ~125/day pre-war; the FY guide of 10.5-11% needs ~14-15% Q4 margin on customer compensations, so a trim toward or below the low end is the main downside on the print, against a consensus already at 10.4%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: guide kept but margin cadence pushed to Q4 and raw-material headwind raised to $110m, stock -3.78. Q4 2025 print (2026 first guide) -4.11. Guidance-cadence news has been sold on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced at the FY level: consensus FY margin 10.4% already sits below the 10.5% low end, so a guide narrowed to 'around 10.5%' is close to neutral. What is not priced is a cut below 10.4% or a larger raw-material number (helium price increases dated July onward land in H2 costs). If the market expected a cut, Q4 consensus margin would sit well below 13.9% and the skew would be put-bid; it is call-bid (-2.83).
findings.independence: Helium: https://apps.digitimes.com/news/a20260625PD216.html (Nippon Sanso +30% from July 2026, snippet), https://energynewsbeat.co/?p=230143 (Hormuz transits mid-Sept, snippet); resin PPI +10.7% to July 2026 https://www.berlinpackaging.com/content/market-insights/Industry-Update-Q3-2026-English.pdf (snippet, notes PE easing). Q1 $90m figure via https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-4-18-autoliv-inc-stock/ (snippet). Counterweight sized in: Valeo confirmed its FY guide on 10-22 in the same cost environment.

findings.finding: Short interest rose to 6.76% of float / 6.2 days to cover at 30 Sept 2026 (up 7.3% on the prior record and from ~2.5% / 3.1 days a year earlier) while the Q3 EPS consensus was cut from ~$2.26 (July) to $2.18 (Oct 19), so the bar has been lowered and shorts have built for a guide disappointment; a held guide meets a short base that needs ~6 days of volume to cover.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print in the baseline carried this level of short interest; the two up-reactions (Q1 2025 +5.56, Q1 2026 +6.82) both came on prints that cleared a lowered bar after a weak tape.
findings.why_not_priced: The 25d skew already pays upside (-2.83) and the stock ran +4.7% in five sessions into the print, so part of a cover is likely done or priced; this finding is the residual squeeze mechanism if the guide holds. If fully priced, short interest would have fallen into the print rather than risen at the last record.
findings.independence: Consensus drift from Autoliv's consensus page snapshots (https://www.autoliv.com/investors/consensus-estimates vs the July 22 snapshot via https://www.autoliv.com/es/node/565, snippet). Baseline skew and run-up are independent market data pointing the same way.

findings.finding: Valeo, reporting Q3 sales on 2026-10-22 in the same input-cost environment, confirmed its FY2026 guidance and said H2 operating margin and FCF will be at least H1 levels, with Q4 sequential growth in line with seasonality; a peer that holds a margin guide the day before is weak evidence that Gulf-driven cost inflation has not broken European supplier guides.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No cited history of ALV trading on a peer's guide; Q2 2026 ALV kept its own guide and fell -3.78.
findings.why_not_priced: Released the evening before; ALV's spot was sealed at 13:09 ET on 10-22, before or around Valeo's release. Reuters reported Valeo's sales slightly below the €4.93bn consensus, so the read is mixed and small.
findings.independence: Same Valeo document as the LVP finding (different line). Reuters via https://www.globalbankingandfinance.com/valeo-posts-lower-sales-auto-industry-weakness-persists/ on the sales miss cuts against it.

findings.finding: GM's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-20) shows GM North America wholesales of 870k against 840k a year earlier (+3.6%) and a FY EBIT-adjusted guide narrowed to $14.5-15.5bn with the $15.0bn midpoint unchanged, a firmer North American customer read than the ~-5% NA LVP implied by Valeo's table, relevant to Autoliv's weakest region (Americas, 32% of sales).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Americas organic -3.3% (4.9pp under LVP) in Q2 2026 coincided with a -3.78 reaction; no cited history of ALV moving on GM's print.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for two sessions, so likely partly in the +4.7% five-day run-up; one customer, not the industry. Small for that reason.
findings.independence: Cuts against the Valeo-derived NA production figure in the LVP finding; the two are kept separate because one is a single customer's own wholesale number and the other an industry series.

outside_window.finding: Türkiye plant closure: $142m total restructuring, ~$40m annual pretax savings starting 2027, full run-rate 2028.

searched_and_found_nothing: Autoliv company news Aug-Oct 2026: only a dividend (08-13), a virtual-testing PR (09-08), the Q3 call invitation (09-24), the share retirement (09-30) and a research advisory board PR (10-02) via https://www.inderes.fi/en/companies/Autoliv ; no profit warning, no 8-K outside the cadence

September/October 2026 S&P Global Mobility monthly LVP forecast update: not found publicly (July and August updates via autoinformed.com showed Europe, NA, South Asia, Japan up and Greater China down for 2026)
Pre-Q3 analyst rating changes in September 2026 (TD Cowen, Wolfe downgrades claimed by an aggregator): could not date-confirm
Q3 2026 helium spot price index: no dated August/September figure found
IEEPA refund quantification for Autoliv beyond the Q2 call ($12m received, $9m passed to customers): none in the Q2 10-Q visible text

rejected_candidates.candidate: Q3 buyback pace: 1,232,671 shares retired in Q3 (~$145m at ~$118) vs 1.65m / $200m in Q2, within the $300-500m 2026 plan
rejected_candidates.detail: The same share count drives the EPS-bar finding; filing it as a capital-return finding would count one document twice.

rejected_candidates.candidate: RBC 'Hold, $450 target' dated 2026-10-08 on an aggregator
rejected_candidates.detail: Aggregator entry with an implausible target and rating that contradicts RBC's April Outperform; no primary note found, treated as a data error.

rejected_candidates.candidate: IEEPA tariff refund one-off in Q3 (Autoliv booked $12m gross / $3m net in Q2)
rejected_candidates.detail: No Q3 amount sourced; Q2 showed it is largely passed through to customers and Autoliv's tariffs are mostly not IEEPA, so nothing company-level to file.

baseline_tension: Mostly agrees with the option market's mild upside lean (skew -2.83, upside paid) and with the +4.7% five-day run-up, which means the positive half of the evidence is partly priced; it cuts against the name's own history of selling 5 of 7 prints, which is why p_up stays at 51.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; this name sold its record Q3 2025 and its Q2 2026 beat): EPS-bar finding cut from +0.6 to +0.4.
Lesson 5 (proxy, derived regional LVP not published by S&P): LVP finding cut from +0.3 to +0.2.
Lesson 7/3 (positive agrees with an upside-paid skew and a +4.7% run-up, partly priced): positioning finding cut from +0.7 to +0.5.

Left standing: the raw-material/guidance negative (-1.2) already netted for the 10.4% consensus sitting below the guide; short interest was looked up before filing it (6.76% float, not crowded) so no further shrink; GM and Valeo peer reads unchanged at +0.2 each; p_up 51 and abs_move 5.5 unchanged.
